nRulesThing.text:
Group: a thing's page. Rules sit under the lifecycle, one row per rule (1A). Each row says the rule in one sentence, the fields and states it holds in, and what a caller gets when it breaks.
handle has two rules, each owning a refusal. oneNamePerPerson carries its own written sentence, so its row says so (2A, the optional description). profile has one rule that refuses nothing: its row says a break is a defect.
The lifecycle carries no mark for rules (3A). The Errors list says what decides each refusal: a rule, the machine, or the handler.

nRulesOp.text:
Group: an operation's page. Every refusal a rule owns reads as the rule's sentence and links to the rule's row on the thing's page (2A). The spine gains a rules stop between the move and the commit, only for an operation that can break a rule (4A).
claim can break two rules, so it has the stop. release only leaves claimed, so it has none; its other refusals have no rule and no link.
